property_summary: When RState is BELOW_ONE and BASE_RESERVE equals BASE_TARGET, correctRState() must NOT change RState to ONE (i.e. RState remains BELOW_ONE).

After calling buyShares, if getVaultReserve().0 equals getPMMStateForCall()'s B0 (BASE_RESERVE == BASE_TARGET) then R state remains BELOW_ONE (i.e., getPMMStateForCall().R == uint256(PMMPricing.RState.BELOW_ONE)).

If before calling buyShares the pool is in BELOW_ONE and BASE_RESERVE equals BASE_TARGET, then after buyShares the pool's reported BASE_TARGET should remain equal to its BASE_RESERVE (the mutant increases BASE_TARGET when equality held).

When _RState_ is BELOW_ONE and before buyShares the public getPMMStateForCall reports B0 equal to B (target equals reserve), after buyShares the reported B0 must not increase (i.e., new B0 <= reported B0 prior to the call).

If before buyShares the pool is in BELOW_ONE and base target equals base reserve, then after buyShares the reported base target must equal the new base reserve (i.e., B0 == B), never strictly greater than B.

property_summary: Invariant: calling adjustMtFeeRate(...) does not change _BASE_TARGET_ (it remains equal to _BASE_RESERVE_) when _RState_ is BELOW_ONE and _BASE_RESERVE_ == _BASE_TARGET_; the mutant (which uses <=) updates _BASE_TARGET_ in that equality case and thus can change it.

If RState is BELOW_ONE and base reserve equals base target, calling adjustMtFeeRate(x) (any valid x) does not change _BASE_TARGET_ in the correct contract, but the mutant (which uses <=) may update _BASE_TARGET_ when reserves equal targets causing a difference.
